eval-smoke-baseline.success_criteria: the /eval smoke run reports PASS (no metric drop >2% vs the saved baseline)

argv:
code-review-gate has NO portable default.

This gate id resolved, but the skill-bundled default cannot review anything: there is
no model-invocable working-diff reviewer to bind a gate to. /code-review and /review
both carry disable-model-invocation: true, so a skill-kind mapping to either is
unlaunchable -- and because verify-gates.md has the orchestrator judge a skill gate
'from its output', an unlaunchable skill gate is indistinguishable from a passing one.
That silent pass shipped twice (2026-07-26 and its remap). This deliberate failure is
the fix: a gate you cannot run must be loud, not green.

Define it in <project>/.claude/eval-gates.json. Project entries win over these
defaults, so a local definition makes this message go away. Prefer kind: argv -- an
exit code cannot be self-attested. Worked example (example-project, 2026-07-28):

  "code-review-gate": {
    "kind": "argv",
    "argv": ["bash", "scripts/session-quality-gate.sh"],
    "cwd": ".", "timeout": 900
  }

That script lints, type-checks and import-checks the Python the session actually
changed -- detected from the WORKING TREE, because verify gates run before
post_session commits, so any committed-delta detection sees nothing and passes.
If the session genuinely needs an LLM review, make it a require_evidence artifact
instead of a gate.
code-review-gate.success_criteria: FAILS BY DESIGN until the project defines code-review-gate in its own .claude/eval-gates.json. There is no portable reviewer to default to, and a gate that cannot run must be loud rather than green. The id is kept in the bundled vocabulary so existing plans still BUILD (build_plan.py rejects unknown gate ids); only execution fails, with instructions.
code-review-gate._note: REWRITTEN 2026-07-28. Was kind: skill -> `code-review`, which is disable-model-invocation and cannot be launched by any agent: silently unrunnable for every session that declared it and had no project-local override. A 2026-07-26 project-side remap to skill `review` reproduced the bug (same flag, and `review` is a routing alias, not a reviewer). Reproduced live 2026-07-27: the same probe plan returned invoke-skill/code-review from outside a .claude root and run-argv from inside a project that defines the gate locally -- i.e. every plan built outside a .claude root inherited the silent no-op.

test-orchestrate.success_criteria: all tests pass (exit-zero outcome from test-orchestrate); any remaining failure is a gate failure that triggers rework

llm-review-low.success_criteria: exit 0. Runs `claude -p "/code-review low" --output-format json` against the session's WORKING-TREE diff and parses the reviewer's findings block. PASS REQUIRES A PARSEABLE, EMPTY FINDINGS BLOCK -- exit 0 from the CLI is NOT enough. Three outcomes: 0 = empty findings block; 1 = >=1 finding; 2 = INDETERMINATE (no parseable block after one retry, or empty/invalid stdout, or is_error). 2 is a FAILURE, never a pass: a headless session can exit 0 having emitted nothing, and a gate that cannot tell 'no findings' from 'no output' is the silent-green bug this framework already shipped twice. Intent-into-review: PLAN_EXECUTE_INTENT_FILE (or --intent-file) feeds the session's ## Work text to the reviewer inside UNTRUSTED-DATA markers so a deliberate choice classifies ask-user; the exit code is computed from the findings count alone, so intent can only downgrade an action, never clear a finding.
llm-review-low._note: ADDED 2026-08-12 (plan-framework-upgrade s10, RV-01) on the strength of s01's BINDABLE probe verdict, which proved main-tree AND in-worktree binding -- both matter, because isolated parallel-group members run their gates inside their own worktree. PROVEN BEFORE INSTALL, not asserted: fixtures/llm-review-gate/rerun.sh plants an off-by-one, runs every INSTALLED level, and exits non-zero if the plant is missed, if the clean allow-control fails, if an intent block claiming the bug is deliberate clears it, or if any of the three captured INDETERMINATE responses (empty result / conversational summary with no findings block / zero-byte stdout, all exit 0) passes. The harness runs under the same restricted env allowlist run_deploy_argv imposes in production. Distinct from code-review-gate ON PURPOSE: that id is the DETERMINISTIC pytest/lint gate and is not overloaded. TIMEOUTS are 4x the slowest wall measured on a ~10-line fixture diff (31s at this level); a real multi-file diff reviews slower, so if this ever times out raise it from a MEASURED run rather than guessing -- a timeout arrives in the feedback file as one line and is indistinguishable from a real finding.
